subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth embedded dispatch be a provider or CLI-backend capability consumed by generic core routing, or should core permanently own the claude-cli allowlist and public eligibility API?
rationale: Both designs can fix the observed bug, but they establish different long-term provider ownership and PluginRuntime compatibility contracts that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Make eligibility provider-owned
options.body: Add a generic backend capability for subscription-safe embedded dispatch and keep Claude-specific auth policy in the Anthropic or claude-cli owner boundary.

options.title: Approve the core exception
options.body: Keep the core claude-cli allowlist and PluginRuntime helper as an explicitly approved narrow exception with compatibility tests and documented ownership.

options.title: Narrow to active-memory only
options.body: Pause the general PluginRuntime API and implement a smaller owner-approved active-memory path until a reusable dispatch contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Make eligibility provider-owned
recommendation.body: Add a generic backend capability for subscription-safe embedded dispatch and keep Claude-specific auth policy in the Anthropic or claude-cli owner boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Active Memory work and documented CLI/plugin ownership span both sides of the decision.
